previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted for acute kidney injury in the setting of one week of watery diarrhea. Initial evaluation revealed prerenal azotemia likely due to dehydration from diarrhea. She was found to have Clostridium difficile infection, treated with oral vancomycin and metronidazole after initial IV therapy due to symptom recurrence. A concurrent asymptomatic Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary tract infection was treated with ceftriaxone, later switched to oral ciprofloxacin based on sensitivities. Her Myfortic was held during infection to reduce immunosuppression. Transaminases rose during admission, likely due to recurrent hepatitis C, requiring outpatient monitoring. Renal function improved with IV hydration and supportive care, though creatinine remained above baseline. Lower extremity edema persisted, with echocardiogram showing moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension, prompting cardiology referral. She was discharged home on antibiotics, with instructions to hold Lasix and Myfortic until further follow-up, and with medication adjustments including metoprolol dosing and anticoagulation prophylaxis.

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with a history of HCV cirrhosis 
s/p liver transplant (course complicated by rejection and 
recurrent HCV) who is  admitted for acute kidney injury.  

Of note, Ms. ___ was recently hospitalized with an elevated 
creatinine of 3.7 from a baseline of 1.6-2.0. Although she had 
marked lower extremity edema, she did not display other signs of 
volume overload. Given her BUN:Cr ratio, prerenal physiology 
secondary to diarrhea/deyhdration was the most likely etiology 
of her renal failure. She was bolused  with IV fluids, Lasix was 
held, and her creatinine slowly  improved. On ___, in the 
setting of worsening diarrhea, her  creatinine bumped up 
slightly, but improved again with  additional IVF and treatment 
of her underlying diarrheal illness. Her creatinine improved to 
2.3 by the time of discharge which was not quite at baseline. 
Most likely there was also a component of ATN which will take 
longer to improve.  Her hospital course was also notable for C. 
diff and a klebsiella UTI. For her C. diff, she was discharged 
on vanco and flagyl. She completed a course of Cipro for the 
UTI. Given the patient's substantial volume issues, her lasix 
was not restarted upon discharge. Her myfortic was discontinued 
given her active infections.  

Since discharge, the patient states that her diarrhea has 
markedly improved. She is having ___ bowel movements per day. 
However, she continues to have low energy and appetite. Where 
she used to drink 5 bottles of water daily prior to her previous 
admission, she is only drinking ___ bottles of water per day.

Brief Hospital Course:
REASON FOR ADMISSION
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with a history of HCV cirrhosis 
s/p liver transplant, who has had a course complicated by 
rejection and recurrent HCV infection. She was recently admitted 
for ___, C. diff diarrhea, and urinary tract infection. She is 
now readmitted with elevated creatinine. 

ACTIVE ISSUES
1. Acute on chronic kidney injury: Patient's elevated creatinine 
was most likely secondary to prerenal physiology because her 
creatinine rapidly normalized with IVF. This could be due to 
recently decreasing her PO intake vs. tacrolimus toxicity.  
However, her BUN:Cr ratio was not classically prerenal and an 
element of ATN from her prior presentation is a possibility. We 
also considered AIN given patient is on omeprazole and had rare 
urinary eosinophils during her prior admission, but urinary 
eosinophils are currently negative. Nonetheless, her ompeprasole 
was transitioned to ranitidine. Her tacrolimus dose was 
decreased (goal ___. Protein/Cr ratio was 1.0. On ___, patient 
had a renal ultrasound that suggested right renal artery 
stenosis. This will require follow-up as an outpatient with 
Nephrology. Patient's providers have also been concerned that 
she is not keeping up with PO intake at home and would benefit 
from additional home services, given her frequent admissions. A 
home safety evaluation and VNS is being arranged. 

2. Transaminitis: Patient's AST/ALT and Alk phos have remained 
elevated since her recent discharge. Because her myfortic was 
stopped during her last admission, we considered rejection. 
Recurrent HCV is also possible. Patient had a repeat liver 
ultrasound that did not show evidence of obstruction or 
thrombosis. Her enzymes trended down without intervention. 

3. Diarrhea: Patient diagnosed with severe C. difficile during 
recent admission, on metronidazole and PO vancomycin and was 
scheduled to complete a 14 day course of the antibiotics on 
___. Given patient's report of feeling off-balance, her 
metronidazole was discontinued, and feelings of off-balance 
improved. She was continued on PO vancomycin. We continued to 
hold her Myfortic. 

4. Gait imbalance: Patient described a sensation of falling to 
the left side while walking, which began after her recent 
discharge. Her exam showed difficulty with tandem gait but 
Romberg, rapid-alternating movements, and finger-to-nose 
remained intact. Metronidazole was discontinued and sensation 
improved. Her difficulty with tandem gait should be followed-up 
as an outpatient. 
 
5. Essential tremor: Most likely a side effect of tacrolimus. 
Dose was decreased as above. Because patient has proteinuria, 
she unfortunately is not able to switch to sirolimus. She was 
continued on topiramate and metoprolol. 
  
CHRONIC ISSUES
1. HCV cirrhosis s/p OLT on ___: Patient presented with 
slightly worsening liver function as above. Her tacrolimus was 
decreased to target a goal trough of ___. She remained off of 
myfortic due to C. dif infection. Home diuretics were held. She 
was continued on Bactrim prophylaxis. 

2. Lower extremity edema: Patient has chronic lower extremity 
edema. This may be related to immunosuppression. A recent 
echocardiogram showed a preserved EF but severe tricuspid regurg 
and pulmonary HTN, so it is also likely that lower extremity 
edema is secondary to R heart failure. Recommend outpatient 
Cardiology evaluation. 
 
3. Type II DM: Patient was maintained on glargine and insulin 
sliding scale. 

4. Seizure disorder: Patient was continued on topiramate and 
gabapentin.  

5. HTN: Continued amlodipine

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___, 

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your stay here at 
___.

Your were admitted for an decrease in your kidney function 
likely secondary to dehydration.  We gave you IV fluids and this 
resolved.  We also changed your omeprazole to ranitidine as the 
former may have been affecting your kidneys.  Your kidney 
function returned to normal but we want you to follow up with 
the kidney doctors as your kidneys are easily irritated and 
spill protein into the urine.  

In addition, we are concerned that your tacro levels are too 
high and may be contributing to your tremor.  We lowered your 
dose during this admission and hope that this will improve.

You reported a sensation of feeling off balanace and dizzy.  We 
think this may be a result of metronidazole you were prescribed 
for your diarrheal infection and the high tacro levels.  We 
stopped the metronidazole and decreased your tacro dosing.

The following changes were made to your medication regimen: 
START ranitidine for heartburn
DECREASE tacrolimus to 1mg twice daily
STOP metronidazole
STOP omeprazole as this may have been interacting with your 
kidneys
CONTINUE vancomycin to finish a 14 day course

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with hepatitis C cirrhosis status post liver
transplant now with transaminitis.

COMPARISON:  Abdomen ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no biliary dilatation seen in the transplanted liver.  The
extrahepatic common duct is normal measuring 4 mm.  No fluid collection is
seen in the right upper quadrant.  The spleen is normal measuring 11.3 cm.  No
hydronephrosis is seen on limited views of the kidneys.

DOPPLER EXAMINATION:  Color Doppler and spectral waveform analysis was
performed.  The main, right and left portal veins are patent with hepatopetal
flow.  Appropriate arterial waveforms with are seen in the main, right and
left hepatic arteries.  The hepatic veins and IVC are patent.

IMPRESSION:

1. Patent hepatic vasculature.

2. Normal appearance of the liver with no biliary dilatation.

HISTORY:  Acute on chronic renal insufficiency.

COMPARISON:  Renal ultrasound ___, CT ___,
abdominal ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS: The right kidney is 8.6 cm and the left kidney is 11.1 cm, unchanged
in size from ___. The difference in size may be due to kidney
position as seen on CT ___. There is no hydronephrosis, stone, or mass
identified.

DOPPLER:  Doppler assessment of the renal vasculature was performed.  The
bilateral main renal arteries are patent with forward flow in diastole.  The
bilateral renal veins are patent.

On the right, there is slight tardus parvus in the upper, mid, and lower poles
with the RI's of 0.79, 0.81 and 0.78, respectively.  In the left upper, mid,
and lower pole poles, there is brisk systolic upstroke with forward flow in
diastole with RI's of 0.77, 0.80, and 0.76, respectively.

The study is performed with a full, normal appearing bladder.

IMPRESSION:
1. No hydronephrosis.  

2. Slight tardus parvus in the right intrarenal arteries, suggesting right
renal artery stenosis, although stenosis is not seen on CT ___. 

3. Patent main renal arteries and veins. Normal left renal Doppler.
